desc1: Visual Arts Society provides students with opportunities to explore and develop their creativity.
desc2: In general, our society members participate in creative activities, share ideas, and showcase their artwork while building artistic skills and confidence. In this term, we will cooperate with Jeju recycling center(제주 새활용센터) and assign members of our society to  art pieces with rubbish individually.
desc3: Our imagination and creativity to express ourselves through art.

desc1: Our society combines mixed media art with digital art, allowing students to express themselves through art in a personal and comfortable way.
desc2: We teach students how to utilize popular digital art tools such as procreate and also teach them mixed media, a very prominent and evolving type of art in the current digitalised world.
desc3: We are the only branched type of art society, and we accept all year groups with ease, as each student can start at their own level, unlike Visual Art that is very restrictive and harder to master.

desc1: Visualise Society is a creative society focused on design, artistic inventions, and innovative thinking. Our purpose is to give students a space where they can turn their ideas and imagination into real projects. We encourage members to look at everyday problems from different perspectives and develop creative solutions through designing and creating artistic inventions. Rather than focusing only on the appearance or technical function of a product, we aim to create ideas that are meaningful, practical, and useful to people. The society welcomes students with different interests and encourages collaboration, experimentation, and independent thinking. Ultimately, Visualise Society aims to help students see the world differently and turn what they imagine into something real.
desc2: Members will have the opportunity to develop their own creative ideas through design and artistic invention. We will support students in turning their ideas into real projects through brainstorming, designing, prototyping, and improving their work. Throughout the year, members will also explore different design and invention competitions taking place in 2026/27 and work towards participating in selected competitions. Unlike traditional engineering projects, our focus will be on combining artistic creativity with invention, allowing members to consider both how something works and how it communicates an idea or experience. Our goal is to give students a space to experiment, create, and develop their ideas into meaningful and innovative outcomes.
desc3: What makes Visualise Society special is that we go beyond traditional art and engineering. While creativity is an important part of our society, we also focus on artistic inventions that combine creative expression with practical problem-solving. Members are encouraged to identify problems in everyday life, think from different perspectives, and create their own inventions or designs to address them. Rather than focusing purely on technical function, we explore how artistic ideas can make inventions more meaningful, engaging, and useful. We will also support members in developing their projects for design and invention competitions in 2026/27, giving them the opportunity to take their ideas beyond the classroom and into the wider world.

society-secretary: Yunchae Sophia Park, Songhyeon Raphaella Shin
desc1: Sonitas is a music society that organizes performances, builds easier approaches to music and explore the depths of music by exploring different genres.
desc2: Analysis of artists who made great contributions to creating the current music culture. Also, the society organizes student-led music performances which explores a large variety of genres
desc3: We are the only music society in our school and it is one of the longest running societies

desc2: Analysis of artists who made great contributions to creating the current music culture. Also, the society organizes student-led music performances which explores a large variety of genres
desc3: We are the only music society in our school and it is one of the longest running societies

desc1: Dance Society is a welcoming society which provides opportunity for both younger and older students to participate in various performances, services, and activities. Dance Society aims to encourage dancers to grow, make relationships with different people, challenge themselves, and discover new styles of dance.
desc2: The dance buskings include various genres including kpop, hiphop, wackking, and contemporary. It happens during Arts Festivals and Dance Enrichment Weeks, which provides an opportunity to showcase our talented dancers to the school community and raise awareness of dance as a both commercial and artistic form.
desc3: The Dance Society is not just a group of students, but a community. We build relationships and grow the same passion for dance among our community. We respect and celebrate each other's talent and differences, and that is how we build our special community.

desc1: Drama Society is about bringing drama into people's everyday lives, not just for those who've always seen themselves as performers. We want to break down the awkwardness or hesitation people often feel around drama, and build a space where anyone can get involved, whether through performing, backstage work, or bringing their own ideas to life.
desc2: The dance service to Vision Regional Children's Center, aims to teach dance to children who didn't have the opportunity to learn dance. Not only the Society gives a local benefit, but the service provides the students as well to learn and develop their leadership skills in their process.The Dance Society CCA runs during the academic year, and it is run by our own leadership members, to teach younger students choreography and give feedback sessions. This doesn't just act as a learning session, but builds a community of dancers inside the school, fostering the sense of belonging and providing a safe space for dancers to explore themselves as a dancer.
desc3: What makes us special is that we don't expect you to already be "a drama person." Whether you've performed for years or have never set foot on a stage, there's a place for you.

desc1: The whole purpose of English Society is to provide a safe space where students can comfortable harness their full potential in regards to speaking and studying English. We help them write pieces, talk about different ideas in English, different Literature forms such as poetry, and even encourage school students to enter different competitions hosted by international branches.
desc2: 1. Talk about different topics (including news) in English, 2. Studying different Literature and Language forms (class-related and personal interests), 3. Different English competitions, 4. Presentations
desc3: ENGSOC is the first society to focus on a universal topic that is highly important in our school NLCSJ. We promote the main language of learning in a fun way and we are a society that is easy to join and highly accessible for all year groups.

desc1: Training students to participate in competitive debate and fostering a spirit of rational discourse
desc2: Mock debates with feedback from the chairs, lectures on major debate-related topics (e.g. environment, criminal law, etc)
desc3: Only society based not on a specific academic subjects but on the skills underlying good academics

desc1: The European Language Society is a community for students who are interested in European languages, cultures, and the connections between them. Our society aims to create an enjoyable and welcoming environment where members can explore languages beyond the classroom and develop a deeper appreciation for European cultures. Through language, we hope to encourage communication, cultural understanding, and curiosity about the wider world. Whether members are already studying a European language or simply interested in learning something new, everyone is welcome to join and discover the diversity and richness of Europe.
desc2: Our society offers a variety of engaging activities that allow members to explore European languages and cultures in an interactive way. Older students studying languages such as Spanish and French will lead introductory lessons and activities, giving younger students the opportunity to learn useful vocabulary, phrases, and basic expressions. We will also organise culture-sharing sessions where members can explore different European countries through their traditions, food, music, everyday life, etc. During Enrichment Week, we hope to organise additional language and cultural activities that allow members to explore European cultures in a more immersive and engaging way. Through these activities, members can learn from one another and develop a deeper appreciation for different languages and cultures.
desc3: What makes us special is that we create a space where students can learn languages from one another while exploring the cultures behind them. Rather than focusing only on traditional language learning, our society combines student-led lessons with interactive cultural sharing. Older students can share their knowledge and experiences with younger students, creating a supportive environment where everyone can learn regardless of their language ability. Members also have the opportunity to explore different aspects of European culture beyond the classroom. Through this combination of language learning, cultural exploration, and peer-led activities, we hope to make learning European languages enjoyable, accessible, and meaningful for everyone.

desc1: As a whole, Latin & Classics Society aims to foster a kind and supportive environment for individuals to explore their classical passions. In particular, our society encourages and enable active discussions among like-minded classicist. From philology, literature, history, archaeology, to even philosophy, our society is concerned with all things classical. Specifically, the aims and objectives of this academic year’s Latin Society are twofold: a) To ensure Latin Society acts in accordance with SEC’s aims by regularly producing evidence of society’s productivity b) To engage with and appreciate the diverse range of interests of our members, and to provide more opportunities to explore individual interests
desc2: Lang & Lit (2 weeks): Short extracts + discussions Grammar clinics History & Culture (2 week): Interesting article/piece + discussion Certamen/Quiz Progress check (1 week): Time to work on magazine/written output Opportunity for student-led initiatives/presentations
desc3: Unlike other societies, Latin & Classics society involves and allows for much interdisciplinary academic exploration. Given the broad nature of classical studies, our society meetings regularly cover topics ranging from linguistics, literature, history, and even ethical debates! As long as it takes place in the classical world, our society welcomes all kinds of academic topics for debates and activites.

society-secretary: Xuan Chou, Shiya (Ruby) Wang, Haolin Li
desc1: The Mandarin Society serves as a platform for the representation of chinese culture within the school as well as the promoting of the mandarin language to international students through the peer networking system.
desc2: In terms of our long-term projects, we organise the numerous Chinese-culture-oriented events of both the Senior and Junior School. These events have been consistently highly successful, and their smooth operation is entirely thanks to the society members, our link teachers, and our parent group. On a daily basis, we practise our Mandarin skills, with peer mentoring for Mandarin learners while also offering new Chinese students, particularly those new to NLCS or in year 7 assistance through our buddy system.
desc3: We are one of the biggest societies in NLCS, and yet everyone is deeply involved with what we are doing. This is not only reflected in our attendance rate but also in the impact we have on the school community.
link-teacher: Ms. Jenny Liu, Ms. Yuanyuan Cai

desc1: Our society aims to promote cultural exchange and strengthen connections between Korean and international members of our school community. As one of the school’s longest-running societies, we have a strong history of creating opportunities for students and teachers to learn from one another. Our main purpose is to support international teachers in understanding and engaging with Korean culture, while also encouraging students to take an active role in sharing their culture and experiences. Through educational resources, cultural activities, and opportunities for interaction, the society aims to create a welcoming environment where both Korean and international members can learn from and connect with each other. Our core target is to foster the everlasting passion and love towards the Korean language and literature.
desc2: The society currently focuses on two main activities. First, members are developing a teaching resource designed to help international teachers in understanding aspects of Korean culture. The first draft of this resource is expected to be completed around December. Second, the society participates in Korean Enrichment Week by running a booth where students can share Korean culture and interact with the wider school community. In the future, we also hope to bring back our 1:1 tutoring programme, which connects students with international teachers. As the society grows, this programme can be developed further when older student leaders are able to coordinate tutors and schedules.
desc3: What makes our society special is its long history and its focus on creating meaningful connections between Korean and international members of our school community. Rather than simply learning about different cultures, our activities allow students and teachers to actively share their own experiences and learn from one another. We also give students the opportunity to take responsibility for projects that have a real impact on the school community, such as developing resources for international teachers and organising activities during Korean Enrichment Week. In the future, we hope to build on this foundation by bringing back our 1:1 tutoring programme and expanding opportunities for cross-cultural interaction, which is not usually seen around a multitude of societies and is thus a proud and unique aspect of our society.

desc1: The purpose of our society is to foster engagement with history in the school, while also allowing those who are already interested in history to delve deeper into the subject. History is something that is relevant to many different fields, and it sometimes even helps us with the understanding of the current issues. Taking advantage of the unique location of our school, our society also aims to explore the history of Jeju, helping to understand how it was shaped to the area that it currently is. Furthermore, I want to make the members and students outside of the society realize that history is not just about what happened in the past, but about our own interpretation of it, and learning from what came before us.
desc2: Activities will widely depend on the personal interests of the members of the society. We will present short presentations of events that happened in the past. But rather than focusing on the ‘lectures,’ we will center it more on what individual members of the society can find out on their own. To do this, I will organize numerous activities during the meeting times, including mock trials (putting historical figures on trial), having a movie screening (and discuss how effectively or accurately the movie portrayed the moment in time), looking at different interpretations of the same event and having a discussion afterwards, or sharing about an unknown historical event or person. Furthermore, during enrichment weeks, I want to host a competition where students can write or perform short letters or monologues in the perspective of different stakeholders of a historical event. If possible, we could collaborate with a museum to allow a couple of selected winners’ monologues to be displayed or showcased along with sweets to keep the contestants motivated. This type of event, I believe, will allow students to understand that history is shaped by interpretation. That every individual will perceive an event differently, through their own lens.
desc3: The reason this society is special is because it allows us to take a step back in this fast-paced society and learn from things that happened in the past. It allows students to engage with different events from the past and possibly use it to help them.

desc1: The Geography Society is a community dedicated to explore the relationship between people, places and the fascinating environment. Our core purpose of this society is to give student intellectual fun as well as bridging the knowledge to geographical studies and real world applications. We welcome any one, regardless of their year group, major, as long as they have a passion for geography. In geography, we have various topics that frame inside the subject geography such as physical landscapes, sustainability and up to earthquakes and tsunamis. Our society also aims to build a supportive network of passionate people who wants to make an impact on the world.
desc2: Our society hosts diverse programs designed to offer activities that match both academic and social interests. For example, our former chairs has associated different activities which our students would choose, so it would highly depend on what the students want to do, not us just sharing information and reading out slides, which would be boring. This academic year, we decided to dive deeper in to hands-on activities, such as quizzes, geography-themed trivia etc. Also, infrequently, we would do very memorable and fun experiments such as building architecture that would sustain earthquakes.
desc3: Our society is a small, tight-knit community where we share ideas easily, and make a comfortable, never a pressuring or high outcome focused atmosphere. We create an environment where students are feeling free to share ideas, collaborate on studies, build friendships regardless of year groups. We turn everyday classes to intellectual hubs where you could take a break, connect with fellow geography enthusiasts, talking about global trends/issues.

desc1: The Environmental Stewardship Society serves as the connecting bridge between the NLCS community and the Jeju environment we live in. Despite having the privilege of being located in this unique Jeju environment, not a lot of students have the opportunity to explore it to the fullest extent. Our society aims to narrow that gap and encourage students to engage with the environment that is given to them. Furthermore, we aim to help raise awareness of the extent to which Jeju is affected by various environmental pressures. We will also engage in various initiatives to mitigate these environmental effects.
desc2: Our society will explore environmental issues through a combination of research, practical modeling, and volunteering. Members will research topics such as environmental damage, sustainability, and ways to reduce human impact on nature. We will then apply our knowledge by creating models and prototypes that demonstrate environmental mechanisms and solutions, allowing students to understand these concepts through hands-on activities. We also plan to participate in volunteering and environmental activities outside of school, where members can contribute directly to the local community and environment. Through these activities, we hope to develop both our understanding of environmental issues and our responsibility towards protecting the Earth.
desc3: We are a society that focuses on saving what we damaged, Earth. By researching about the various damages and thinking about how we can actually reduce these harms, we encourage the students to engage more in how to help save the world. While some societies may focus on academics or creativity, we aim to participate more in how we can benefit the society. Through this, we hope that students who join the society will not only gain academic knowledge but also develop a sense of responsibility for their actions and their impact on the Earth.

desc1: The Southeast Asia Society is a student-led community that explores the cultures, histories, societies, and contemporary issues of Southeast Asia. The society aims to create a space for students to learn about the region, exchange perspectives, and develop a greater understanding of its diversity and global significance. It brings together students with different backgrounds and interests while encouraging curiosity, cultural awareness, and meaningful discussion.
desc2: The society organizes a range of student-led activities centered around Southeast Asian culture and current affairs. These include discussions, educational activities, cultural events, collaborative projects, and opportunities for members to share their own perspectives and experiences.
desc3: What makes the Southeast Asia Society special is its ability to bring together different perspectives around a region that is both highly diverse and increasingly significant globally. Rather than focusing on a single country or culture, the society encourages members to consider the connections and differences across Southeast Asia.

desc1: The Economics and Business Management Society is a society that explores the foundations and applications underlying the field of economics, and ways to apply those pieces of knowledge in managing businesses. Economics and business management, despite having numerous quantitative characteristics, are placed under the category of social science, a type of science that deals with the decisions people make based on their values and judgements. As such, through active discussions to share our perspectives on these two fields, we aim to  not only broaden our understanding, but also create our very own ‘economic’ environment where economically rational students exchange perspectives.
desc2: The activities that will take place throughout the 2026-27 academic year will mostly be centred around all members taking unique approaches to expand the boundaries of economics and business management through academic writing and presentation based on interdisciplinary connections. Specifically, we aim to provide all students with sufficient guidance and resources to produce their own articles, give them an opportunity to verbally share their articles through a presentation-based competition, and perhaps educate even younger students to foster financial literacy amongst adolescents. All activities will be actively supported by our school’s economics staff, Ms Paliwal and Mr Gibbard.
desc3: What makes us special amongst other societies is our emphasis on guidance for self-driven and independent exploration of the field. Rather than simply studying and discussing established economic theories, members are encouraged to contribute to the society by deciding an economics-related topic of their own interest and intensively studying that topic to explore the different ways to view economics and business management. We are also special in that we connect these ideas to financial decision-making, by which we are able to draw the most apparent connection between academics and practical actions.

desc1: The Philosophy Society is a student-led space where members explore philosophical issues through discussions and debates. We also organize philosophy-related activities and games to make philosophical ideas more engaging and accessible. In the past, we have also held philosophy interview sessions with teachers, allowing members to explore different perspectives and experiences.
desc2: Activities include group discussions and debates on philosophical issues, philosophy games and interactive activities, and exploring philosophical ideas through different forms of media. We also organize special sessions, such as interviews with teachers about their personal perspectives on philosophical questions. Members are encouraged to share their own ideas, question different viewpoints, and engage in open discussions with others.
desc3: What makes our society special is our ability to make complex philosophical issues approachable and relevant. Rather than discussing philosophical ideas only in abstract terms, we connect them to real-life situations and examples that students can easily relate to. This allows members to understand deeper and sometimes difficult questions without feeling overwhelmed by them. Through discussions, games, and interactive activities, we aim to show that philosophy is not something distant or purely theoretical, but something that can be found in everyday life.

desc1: The society is designed to support students who feel unprepared for TOK, as well as those who want to explore epistemology and critical thinking beyond the classroom. Through discussion, guidance, and practice, we seek to build confidence and curiosity in all members. Ultimately, the society prepares students for the TOK course in Sixth Form while encouraging broader intellectual growth, creativity, and independent thinking.
desc2: Activities in the society are designed to make critical thinking and epistemology interesting and easy to approach. Members take part in short debates, thought experiments, and real-life case studies that encourage them to question ideas and consider different perspectives. We also explore TOK-style questions and connect them to everyday life and other school subjects. The focus is not on getting the “right” answer, it is on creating a relaxed space where students can share ideas, challenge each other and become more confident thinkers.
desc3: What makes us special is that there is no single right answer and no special skill is needed to join. All you need is your own opinion, curiosity, and a willingness to share ideas and hear different perspectives.

desc1: The Neuroscience Society aims to introduce students to the fascinating and rapidly developing study of the brain, cognition and human behaviour. Although neuroscience can seem highly specialised, it connects naturally with fields such as biology, psychology, medicine, engineering and artificial intelligence. Our society explores not only how the brain functions, but also how differences between individual brains influence the way people think, learn, communicate and experience the world. We hope to make neuroscience more accessible while encouraging students to recognise its enormous future potential, from understanding neurodiversity to developing technologies that interact directly with the human brain.
desc2: Our activities are divided into four main areas. First, we hold lectures and discussions exploring both fundamental and highly specialised areas of neuroscience, including neuroimaging, fMRI, neural signalling, cognition and brain-computer interfaces. Second, we collaborate with other STEM societies on practical investigations, such as detecting biological or neural signals and analysing or visualising the resulting data using computers. Third, members can participate in longer-term projects, competitions and research or paper-based investigations into emerging areas of neuroscience and their impact on society. Finally, we explore neuroscience from a wellbeing perspective, particularly neurodiversity, cognition and individual differences, helping promote greater understanding of the different ways in which people think, learn and experience the world.
desc3: What makes the Neuroscience Society special is the extraordinary breadth hidden within such a specialised subject. The brain influences almost every aspect of human life, from learning and emotion to technology, medicine, creativity and social interaction. This allows our society to connect areas that are rarely explored together, combining neuroscience with engineering, AI, psychology, wellbeing and data science. We are also interested not only in how the brain works, but in how differently brains can work. By exploring neurodiversity alongside emerging technologies and scientific research, the society encourages students to see neuroscience not as an isolated subject, but as a field capable of reshaping how we understand both individuals and society.

desc1: The psychology society explores how people think, behave, and interact through engaging discussions and real-world applications. The society provides the members the opportunity to develop thier knowledge on psychology beyond classroom.
desc2: We have lectures and interactive activities that explore interesting case studies. Moreover, we conduct well-known studies to explore how psychology connects to real life.
desc3: The Psychology Society stands out since it brings psychology into everyday life. We look at why people think, feel, and act as they do through discussions, activities, and real-life examples.

desc1: The applied mathematics branch of the Maths Society is a branch that explores the connections between mathematics and various fields of academics and disciplines. This is more specifically done through examining how numbers or quantities are used in the construct or mechanisms of other disciplines, such as economics, engineering, and even philosophy. This specific division of the society allows for discovery in ways that no school curriculum directly deals with. Such discoveries can only be achieved through one’s personal lenses and interests, and through communicating with peers, we aim to expand our lenses to view how expansively mathematics is integrated in many disciplines.
desc2: The applied mathematics branch of the Maths Society has commonly published annual journals called the ‘Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics’ along with the pure mathematics branch. Through the term, we allow all members to come up with a topic of their interest and pursue their topics by writing respective journals. This year, the applied mathematics branch wants to provide students with more intensive resources by dividing the academic year into months that focus on distinctive topics, during which we are planning to host different staff and even external experts to elaborate on the potential tie-ins mathematics may have with different disciplines.
desc3: One thing that makes the maths society special amongst other societies is that we have two branches within one academic field. This allows for students to, first, make a choice in terms of what they wish to focus on within mathematics, and secondly, explore the field with appropriate resources that are matched to their needs. The applied mathematics branch is special in that it centers around the ‘overlaps’ mathematics have with other academic disciplines, which means engaging in our activities will expand students’ interests in not only mathematics but also their key interests.

desc1: The Pure Math Society is a student-led academic community dedicated to exploring mathematics beyond the standard school curriculum. Through weekly sessions, members tackle challenging problems, investigate mathematical concepts, and develop logical and analytical thinking skills. The society encourages students to approach mathematics creatively, focusing not only on finding answers but also on understanding the reasoning behind them. Activities may include problem-solving challenges, mathematical discussions, competitions, and exploration of advanced topics such as number theory, combinatorics, and geometry. By bringing together students with a shared interest in mathematics, the society provides an environment where members can challenge themselves, exchange ideas, and deepen their appreciation of pure mathematics.
desc2: Our activities focus on developing mathematical curiosity, creativity, and problem-solving skills beyond the standard curriculum. We publish JPAM (Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics), a student-led mathematics journal that showcases original investigations, mathematical explorations, and interesting ideas from our community. We also hold regular math discussions, where members explore challenging problems, exchange different approaches, and discuss mathematical concepts in greater depth. Additionally, members participate in weekly projects that encourage independent research, collaboration, and creative applications of mathematics. Through these activities, the society provides students with opportunities to engage with mathematics beyond the classroom and develop a deeper appreciation for mathematical thinking.
desc3: What makes the Maths Society special is its emphasis on mathematics as a form of exploration rather than simply a school subject. We create opportunities for students to investigate ideas that go beyond the curriculum, share different perspectives, and develop their own mathematical interests. Through JPAM, students can publish and engage with original mathematical work, while our discussions encourage collaboration and intellectual curiosity. Our weekly projects further allow members to explore challenging problems independently and creatively. Most importantly, the society brings together students who genuinely enjoy mathematics, creating a community where curiosity is encouraged, difficult ideas are welcomed, and everyone can learn from one another.

desc1: This society aims to help students collaborate to explore physics beyond the regular curriculum or individual research.
desc2: The society activities will include conducting experiments related to various phenomena and  discussing the results altogether for the analysis of its results.
desc3: We provide members with the opportunity to collaborate with students across different year groups, unlike in regular classroom settings.

desc1: The Engineering Society aims to promote engineering within NLCS Jeju and provide students with opportunities to explore engineering beyond the classroom. Engineering is a uniquely interdisciplinary field, combining areas such as physics, mathematics, design, manufacturing, technology, business, and innovation. Our society focuses on understanding how these different disciplines work together to transform ideas into practical solutions. Through lectures, practical activities, discussions, and collaborative projects, we encourage students to develop their creativity, technical understanding, problem-solving skills, and curiosity. Ultimately, the society aims to make engineering accessible, engaging, and applicable to the real world while building a strong engineering community within the school.
desc2: Lectures: The leadership team and society members deliver short lectures on specific areas of engineering and technology. Topics may range from the engineering behind noise-cancelling headphones to aerodynamics, materials, structures, electronics, manufacturing, and other specialised fields. Members are also encouraged to research topics that interest them and share their findings with the society. Practical Activities: Where possible, lectures are followed by practical activities that allow members to apply the concepts they have learned. These activities demonstrate how engineering principles operate in real-life situations and often connect with concepts studied within the IGCSE and IB curricula. The aim is to move beyond theory by allowing students to test, build, observe, and evaluate engineering ideas themselves. Project-Based Activities: The society also undertakes larger collaborative engineering projects. These may involve preparing for engineering competitions or completing internally organised challenges, such as designing and constructing a bridge before testing its strength and performance. Projects allow members to experience the complete engineering process, including research, design, prototyping, testing, evaluation, and improvement.
desc3: What makes the Engineering Society special is the way we connect academic STEM knowledge with real-world application. Rather than studying concepts only in theory, we explore how ideas from physics, mathematics, design, manufacturing, technology, and even business can come together to solve practical problems. Engineering is an exceptionally broad field, which gives our society a high level of flexibility and interdisciplinarity. Almost any idea can be explored under the wider umbrella of engineering, allowing members to connect different interests, experiment creatively, and turn what they learn in the classroom into something tangible, testable, and meaningful.

desc1: This society explores astronomy in multiple facets (observational, theoretical) via presentations, projects, etc.
desc2: We are planning to hold discussion sessions in which members will be able to present an astronomical concept of their choice. The ultimate goal is to create a collection of the concepts presented and also a calendar tracking astronomical events, etc.
desc3: We allow members to not only expand their knowledge in astronomy but apply them to actual collaborative projects and make connections to relevant astronomical events that can be observed.

desc1: The Biology Society brings together passionate students who share a curiosity about the living world, from molecular level to the whole ecosystems. We exist to deepen members' understanding of biology beyond the school curriculum and help students explore career and research pathways in the life sciences. Whether you're passionate about genetics, ecology, medicine, or conservation, anyone who wants to learn, discuss, and get involved in this society is welcomed to join.
desc2: We do a lot of different activities throughout the year, including magazine publications, journal discussions, laboratory workshops, and hands-on practical sessions.
desc3: What sets us apart is our balance of academic depth and genuine community. We're not just a society about biology but we pride ourselves on being inclusive, friendly, and supportive.

desc1: The Medical Society provides opportunities for students interested in medicine and healthcare to explore and develop their passions beyond the classroom. While our society keeps a strong focus on the academic study of medicine, we integrate more engaging, approachable, and accessible activities to allow students to familiarise themselves with medicine. By mixing aspects of medicine that are not always covered directly in the classroom, we allow oppertunities in which students are able to develope a broader understanding of the field and the realities of medicine and healthcare. Ultimately, our goal is not just to support student's interest and expand their knowledge, but to make the study of medicine approachable, familar, and fun.
desc2: The Medical Society does not soley focus on the scientic and achademic aspect of the field, but also offers practical activities that relate to medicine. These include medical-related presentations led by both the leadership team and society members, role play activities of medical senarios, group discussions regarding ethical dilemma or global medical news, as well as hosting lectures from healthcare professionals. Other than the achademic aspect, the Medical Society provides oppertunites for younger students to connect with older students with similar interest for guidance and support.
desc3: The Medical Society exclusively focuses on the field of medicine, exploring content that is beyond the class. Rather than focusing solely on academic aspects of medicine, purely looking at it from a scientific view, we examine its social, ethical, and global aspects of healthcare. In addition, the Medical Society also manages the Medical Review, a student-lead project that delves deeply into a chosen medical topic of research, producing a comprehensive literary article as well as a presentation. Through this project, students can not only gain achademic knowlegde, but also familiarse themselves with professional research papers, presentation skills, communication and cooperation.

desc1: The Veterinary Society focuses on exploring veterinary medicine, animal welfare, and anatomy. It provides students with opportunities to learn about animal anatomy, health, behaviour, and the responsibilities of veterinary professionals through practical activities, and discussions. Overall, it is a place for students interested in animals and veterinary medicine to gain practical knowledge and explore potential careers in the field.
desc2: The Veterinary Society takes part in a variety of activities, including learning about animal anatomy, health and behaviour. Members participate in practical activities such as dissections and observing animal specimens, as well as discussions, presentations, and research into veterinary medicine.
desc3: What makes the Veterinary Society special is that it a space that people with similar intrest which is something i wanted since ive developed this passion. we will also educate them on wat it takes to be a vet as there is alot of variations in a vet(farm, experimental, pet, Exotic Pet). we will teach them things that they cant find like real life examples and we will talk about different real life situations that would help them in the future while increasing their knowledge in the subject.
meetingroom: resting area of B block 3rd floor

desc1: We aim to create a bridge between chemistry and the wider school community by engaging students from all year groups in creative and engaging scientific activities. Beyond the chemistry classroom, we explore interesting areas of chemistry through experiments, demonstrations, challenges, and discussions that encourage students to think scientifically and apply their knowledge to real-world situations. We also introduce younger students to recent developments and innovations in chemistry, helping them understand how the subject continues to shape and respond to changes in the world. Ultimately, we aim to make chemistry enjoyable, accessible, and relevant to students of different ages and levels of experience.
desc2: The Chemistry Society provides students with an opportunity to explore chemistry beyond the classroom through engaging and practical activities. We participate in experiments and demonstrations that allow them to apply chemical concepts in real-life contexts and develop their practical skills. We also explore interesting areas of chemistry that may not be covered in the regular curriculum, including everyday applications, environmental chemistry, and surprising chemical reactions. Through quizzes, discussions, challenges, and collaborative activities, we help members strengthen their understanding of chemistry while working with others who share similar interests.
desc3: What makes our society special is that students can directly experience and explore new chemical concepts through experiments, rather than simply learning about them from textbooks. Our activities allow members to see chemistry in action and understand how abstract concepts work in real situations. We also aim to introduce ideas beyond the regular curriculum, giving students the opportunity to discover areas of chemistry they may not encounter in their lessons. By encouraging students to experiment, question, and explore together, we make chemistry more interactive and memorable. This hands-on approach allows students of different ages and experience levels to develop their curiosity and interest in chemistry.

desc1: The Pharmacy Society introduces students to the science, practice and wider impact of pharmacy beyond the classroom. Our aim is to develop students’ understanding of how drugs are researched, developed, manufactured and used, whilst exploring the links between chemistry, biology and medicine. Students take part in practical activities, including the synthesis of pharmaceutical compounds, and collaborate with the Chemistry Society on educational trips. We also explore current issues through awareness campaigns, such as the environmental impact of plastics in makeup and skincare products. Through monthly research and essay tasks and the production of scientific articles, students develop their research, communication and critical-thinking skills.
desc2: Awareness campaigns Practical work Synthesis of pharmaceuticals Trips (w/ ChemSoc) Article production Monthly research / essay
desc3: What is even Pharmacy? It stems from φάρμακον (phármakon): a drug—poison and remedy—a charm, an enchantment. A time when drugs and magic weren’t clearly distinguished. In fact, it does seem almost magical: one can bring someone back from the brink of death, another can cause it. Fortunately, it is an empirical science, and a multidisciplinary one. Pharmacy is broad; it sits at the intersection of chemistry, biology and medicine. Whether you are interested in becoming a scientist, pharmacist or clinician, pharmacy and pharmaceutical science let you explore how these disciplines intersect; particularly if you are unsure what your scientific interests lie. We offer the opportunity to experience pharmacy as both a science and a real-world profession. Rather than simply learning about drugs, you’ll investigate how pharmaceuticals are synthesised, research current issues and communicate scientific ideas through articles and essays independently. From environmental impacts to pharmacodynamics, we invite you to discover with us.

desc1: We aim to explore and integrate scientific principles that can be applied to uncover the truth behind crime scenes. By developing an understanding of interdisciplinary science, the Forensic Science Society aims to strengthen students’ scientific reasoning, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
desc2: During weekly meetings, we conduct various practicals such as blood splatter pattern analysis and taking finger print. We also develop our inference skills running through various case studies and lectures of specific technique.
desc3: The aspect that makes us special is the interdisciplinary approach to forensic science. Rather than solely focusing on theory, we explore ways to integrate biology, chemistry, and physics, and apply them to real world case analysis. Through hands-on investigations and case studies, we provide opportunity for students to hone their analytical and inference skills.

desc1: The Computer Science society is a group of ambitious students willing to spread their passion for the subject and achieve any CS-related goals/projects.
desc2: Other than preparing for our enrichment week, which would be our main agenda, we are planning to recruit a smaller group of students for a separate project. We will also be starting a journal, where students can write about anything CS-related. (We are open to any other opinions our members may have)
desc3: Because CS is such a broad field, we will be addressing various aspects within the branch to allow our members to potentially find their interests and dive deeper into it. Our weekly meetings will be on a wide range of topics, such that members can find their passion and learn something throughout the year.

desc1: The AI Society is a student-led community dedicated to exploring the rapidly developing field of artificial intelligence. Through discussions, hands-on projects, and collaborative activities, members learn about topics such as machine learning, generative AI, computer vision, and natural language processing. The society encourages students to move beyond simply using AI and instead understand how these technologies work, their real-world applications, and their wider social implications. Members have opportunities to experiment with AI tools, develop their own projects, and share ideas with others. By combining technical learning with creativity and critical thinking, the society provides a space for students to explore the future of technology.
desc2: The AI Society organizes a range of activities designed to help students understand and engage with artificial intelligence. Members contribute to and develop the AI Journal, publishing research, opinions, and explorations of emerging AI technologies and their applications. We also hold regular discussions about AI, where students debate current developments, ethical questions, and the impact of AI on society. In addition, the society hosts lectures on AI and machine learning, introducing students to fundamental concepts, algorithms, and real-world applications. Together, these activities encourage students to explore AI beyond the classroom, develop technical knowledge, think critically, and engage with the rapidly evolving field.
desc3: What makes the AI Society special is its focus on understanding AI from both technical and real-world perspectives. Rather than simply using AI tools, members explore how artificial intelligence and machine learning actually work, while considering their impact on society, education, business, and everyday life. Through the AI Journal, discussions, and expert-style lectures, students can share ideas, question emerging technologies, and explore topics beyond the school curriculum. The society also encourages students to think critically about the opportunities and challenges created by AI. By bringing together students interested in technology, research, and innovation, the society creates a collaborative environment for exploring the future of AI.

desc1: our society is a software development society specialising in website production. Our society comprises design department,programming department and project management department to create an online product: website service.
desc2: We have already had successes with our projects to solve the existing yet unchallenged problems in the school with software engineering. To state a few examples: COSMOS Cloud, COSMOS Houses, COSMOS OneClick, COSMOS QuickScope and more. We create multiple web applications that students and teachers can benefit from.
desc3: Our society is a pioneering society that has competently demonstrated the capabilities of students, who are part of the society, bringing what was originally conceived in our minds to a promising form of software. We have currently collaborated with multiple teachers from various departments including music department, computer science department and even AVPs who had excellent support and feedbacks for our society. Our society is apt for students who wants to be at the forefront of the computer science to innovate and flourish the school into a much better place for everyone. Last but not least, our society, which has multiple departments, provides incredible opportunities for students with different talent to collaborate and make a product. All of the achievements listed above couldn't have been done without the support of programmers, designers and project directors.

desc1: To inform members of how Law impacts daily life and to improve writing and argumentative ability
desc2: Discussions, Lectures, Writing Workshops, Law Journal Practices, activities can be adjusted
desc3: What makes our Law Society special is that we help students build practical skills that are useful both in law and beyond. Through long-form writing, members learn how to structure arguments clearly, research effectively, and communicate complex ideas with precision. Debates, presentations, and discussions strengthen confidence in public speaking and the ability to think quickly under pressure. We also explore how law affects everyday life across areas such as business, technology, politics, healthcare, and human rights, showing its relevance across many careers. By developing writing, speaking, analytical, and research skills, the Society helps prepare students for university, internships, and future professional opportunities.

desc1: Our PE Society is a student led community dedicated to promoting physical education, fitness, wellbeing, and active participation across our school community. We aim to encourage students of all abilities to develop a positive relationship with physical activity while building teamwork, leadership, and confidence. We organise activities and events that give students opportunities to participate, learn new skills, and support one another. We are also willing to support sporting events through supporting refereeing, including volunteering, For example, line judges at KISAC competitions. As Chair, I hope to make the society welcoming and inclusive while encouraging students to take on leadership and volunteering opportunities.
desc2: We organises and participates in a variety of activities that promote fitness, teamwork, leadership, and enjoyment of sport. Activities include recreational sports sessions, fitness challenges, skill-development activities, and opportunities for students to try different sports. The society also supports school sporting events by volunteering in officiating roles, such as refereeing and line judging at KISAC competitions. Members can develop their knowledge of sports rules and gain practical experience while contributing to the wider school sporting community. We also encourage members to suggest and lead activities, helping develop responsibility, communication skills, and confidence through active participation.
desc3: What makes our PE Society special is that we aim to make sport accessible, enjoyable, and meaningful for everyone, regardless of their ability or experience. We are not only focused on playing sport, but also on giving students opportunities to develop leadership, teamwork, and responsibility. Members can take an active role in organising activities and supporting school competitions through opportunities such as refereeing and line judging at KISAC events. This allows students to contribute to the wider sporting community while gaining valuable practical experience. Most importantly, our society brings students together through a shared passion for sport, creating a supportive and inclusive community.
